newsitem.title: CHINA: China urged to strengthen bond market supervision.
newsitem.headline: China urged to strengthen bond market supervision.

text.p: Supervision of China's fledging treasury bond market is lagging behind its development and the government should make increased supervision a priority, a senior official was quoted on Wednesday as saying.

Gao Jian, director of the state debt department of the Finance Ministry, told a meeting of officials of provincial finance departments that the T-bond market had developed very quickly this year due to a series of reforms, the China Securities newspaper said.
China has issued a record 220 billion yuan of treasure bonds and bills so far this year, surpassing the planned 195.2 billion yuan, Gao said.
"But formulating market rules and supervision has lagged behind," Gao said. "From now on, financial authorities at various levels should make this a focus of their work."
Authorities should punish more severely market players who damaged the interests of the state and investors, Gao said.
They should also improve supervision of securities houses, brokerages and clearing houses and uphold the good name of state debt, he was quoted by the newspaper as saying.
